newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Higher on firmer swaps quotes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Higher on firmer swaps quotes.

text.p: Higher swaps quotes have sparked off firmer physical cargo values but traders said the rise might be temporary as demand remained thin.
Near market close, May swaps were quoted at $96.50/$97.50 a barrel, up from Monday's indications at $95.50/$96.50.
May swaps were traded at $96.25 and $96.50 per tonne and balance April at $97.10.
But renewed interest in swaps trade, did not spark off any interest in the physical market.
In the physical market, only one bid was seen at $97 per tonne for May loading supplies against no offers. But the buyer did not lower quotes any further to tempt sellers.
Traders said the cash market were riding purely on swaps strength as buying interest remained lacklustre.
Traders in Hong Kong said China would be looking to North Asia, in particular South Korea for May supplies.
"Freight costs between South Korea and China is at about $7-$8 per tonne, lower than Singapore to China at $8-$10," one trader said.
Bunker demand remained thin as supplies in Singapore were sufficient.
Some sellers remained hopeful that prices would rise later this month when South Korean refinery turnarounds in May starts to bite into supplies.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
